codeql_results.message: A Flask app appears to be run in debug mode. This may allow an attacker to run arbitrary code through the debugger.
Cross-site scripting vulnerability due to a [user-provided value](1).

findings.description: Flask application is running in debug mode, which may expose sensitive information or allow arbitrary code execution through the debugger.
findings.remediation_description: Disable debug mode in production environments to prevent potential information exposure and code execution risks.

findings.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.description: User-provided 'name' parameter is directly embedded into the HTML response without proper escaping, potentially allowing XSS attacks.
findings.novelty_reason: Basic XSS pattern in template injection
findings.remediation_description: Use Flask's built-in escape() function to sanitize user input before rendering in HTML responses.

healing_failures.root_cause: User input is directly embedded in HTML response without escaping
Flask app still running in debug mode in production

report.recommendation: Fix the suspected XSS and debug mode vulnerabilities. Disable debug mode in production and implement proper input escaping for web responses.
